title: Layers of Access Control on a Modern Linux Box
description: A Mermaid flowchart following one read() syscall through three AND-composed Linux access-control gates — DAC, capabilities, and MAC — showing a denied read of /etc/shadow beside an allowed read of a web file.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Trace a single read() syscall through the DAC, capability, and MAC gates.
Explain why the gates are AND-composed and why a single DENY is decisive.
prerequisites: Unix file permissions (owner/group/other), processes and UIDs

instructionalStrategies: Trace the left (denied) and right (allowed) chains side by side, hovering each gate.
Discuss why MAC can deny even when the file owner has granted DAC permission.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why does the shadow read fail at the very first gate?
If DAC permits but MAC denies, which wins, and why is that the safer composition order?

chapter_title: "System Security: OS, Memory, and Access Control"
